statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
neutral_facts: The deceased sustained stab injuries on her neck while in her matrimonial house. Initially, four family members of her in-laws were prosecuted under Sections 498A and 306 of the IPC but were acquitted. Two years later, the brother of the deceased lodged a complaint against six family members of her in-laws, alleging that two of them killed the deceased by stabbing her and the other four caused the disappearance of murder evidence. The accused were prosecuted under Sections 302 and 201 read with Section 34 of the IPC. The trial court relied on the testimony of the deceased's son, a child witness, and convicted two of the accused. The High Court reversed the conviction, disbelieving the child witness's evidence and noting the possibility of suicide. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision, finding the child witness's evidence lacked adequate corroboration and the medical evidence cast doubt on the reliability of the prosecution's case.
